confirmed.statement: S1 explicitly uses a between-subjects randomized AI-allowed/AI-forbidden design. Within each of eight time slots, the lab conditions and each student's computer assignment are randomized.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 2.1, Overview; p. 11, Section 3.3 (time-slot randomization strata); p. 53, Figure A3 notes.

confirmed.statement: S1 assigns permission and access to generative AI during students' own learning and analytical essay writing, rather than assigning whose output they evaluate.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 2.1, Learning Phase; p. 8, Treatment; p. 79, Figures B1-B2 (student ChatGPT exchanges).

confirmed.statement: The supplied tool is a dedicated, logged-in ChatGPT (GPT-4o) account; any generative AI tool is permitted. Free chatbot use includes generating essay text and explaining concepts, supporting the open_chat role.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Section 2.1, Treatment; p. 52, Figure A2 Panel A; p. 79, Figures B1-B2.

confirmed.statement: The AI-forbidden arm prohibits generative AI. Both arms permit standard online resources, including Google, Wikipedia, the college library website, and other websites, as the form describes.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Section 2.1, Treatment; p. 52, Figure A2 Panels A-B.

confirmed.statement: AI assignment is between students, with both original groups assessed without AI or external resources in Session Two. This is an unaided follow-up, so randomized within-person AI-condition order is not required.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 2.1, Overview; p. 9, Section 2.2, Session Two; p. 11, Section 3.3.

confirmed.statement: All knowledge tests prohibit AI. Topic assignment, allocation of the complementary essay prompts across sessions, and Session Two test-versus-essay order are explicitly randomized.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 2.1, Topic Assignment and Baseline Assessment and Learning Phase; pp. 8-9, Post-Learning Test continuation and Section 2.2.

confirmed.statement: The arm counts match: assigned sign-ups are 130 AI-allowed and 126 AI-forbidden; Session One analyzed students are 107 AI-allowed and 104 AI-forbidden.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 36, Table 2, treatment headings and N (Students) row; p. 37, Table 3, N row; p. 61, Table A1, N (Students) row, Used account columns.

confirmed.statement: The form correctly identifies the reported 67.3-percentage-point effect on provided-account use and 1.9-percentage-point effect on other-model use as assignment effects, rather than treated-arm usage rates.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 14, Section 4.1; p. 37, Table 3 Panels A-B, Effect column and notes.

confirmed.statement: The paper reports logged uses for explaining concepts by 57 percent of treated students, drafting responses by 31 percent, and summarizing readings by 17 percent.
Preregistration of S1 is not stated in the saved document. The preregistered trial mentioned in Appendix B.7 belongs to LearnLM Team (2026).

summary: The PDF explicitly supports random assignment to generative-AI access versus prohibition during students' own learning and essay writing. The form's assignment, comparison arm, and tool coding are supported, so criterion 1 holds.
